topic: There is no single Danish quota 2
text:
Quota 1 is national and mechanical: your converted grade average against a published cut-off. Quota 2 is not. The national agency's position is that quota 2 places are allocated "according to criteria published by the institution", which means each institution decides what counts and the criteria genuinely differ between them.

The practical consequence is that there is no general Danish quota 2 strategy to follow, and advice that describes one is describing a single institution. Aalborg states plainly that motivational letters and recommendations are not considered relevant to its quota 2 assessment. Copenhagen Business School requires a motivational essay. Southern Denmark uses an admissions test. Those are three different answers to the same question, all correct, at three universities in one small country.

Check the quota 2 page of the specific programme you want, and treat anything more general than that as background.
attribution: The Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science, with the institutional examples read from each university's own pages
whatThisIsNot: This is not the deadline, and not a suggestion that quota 2 is optional. Applying by 15 March at 12:00 puts you in both quotas automatically if your average converts.
